small_guidance:
- The kernel uses `input_precision="ieee"` which disables TF32 tensor cores — this is the dominant performance loss on 4090. Switch to `input_precision="tf32"` (or remove the arg, default is tf32) for fp32 inputs; this should give 3-5x speedup on the matmul.
- Expand autotune to include larger K tiles (BLOCK_K=64 with num_stages=4) since K=8192 is large and benefits from deeper pipelining; also try BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8 num_stages=4 which is typically optimal for square ~8k GEMMs on Ada.
- Consider pre-transposing weight to (K, N) layout outside the kernel (one-time cost in __init__) so the inner B load is along contiguous N rather than strided across `stride_wn`; current `w_ptrs` uses `offs_n * stride_wn` on the outer K loop which is the non-contiguous axis.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite with split-K or stream-K persistent scheduling: M=N=1024... wait, M=1024, N=8192, K=8192. With BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256 there are only 8*32=256 tiles, which underutilizes the 128 SMs poorly across the K=8192 reduction. A split-K kernel (e.g. SPLIT_K=4) launching 4x more programs that atomically accumulate (or write to a temp + reduce) would expose more parallelism.
- Switch the matmul to use tf32 tensor cores (allow_tf32 semantics) — the reference `nn.Linear` uses cuBLAS which exploits TF32 by default on Ada; an `ieee` fp32 Triton matmul has no chance of beating it. This single change should move fast_p from 0.54 toward 1.5+.
- Store weight transposed once at init (shape [K, N], contiguous on N) so the K-loop loads B with unit-stride on the inner N axis; this enables wider vectorized loads and better L2 reuse across the GROUP_M swizzle.
